mainTopic: The חתן's exemption, רבן גמליאל's unusual conduct in mourning, honor for slaves, and the Sages' personal prayers after תפלה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of why a חתן who marries a בתולה is exempt from קריאת שמע. Only worry that comes from a מצוה exempts a person; a mourner's grief does not. Next comes a new משנה with two stories about רבן גמליאל. He bathed on the night his wife died because he was an אסטניס, and he accepted תנחומין for his worthy slave טבי. The משנה also brings a מחלוקת about whether a חתן may choose to say קריאת שמע anyway. The גמרא explains that mourning at night is only דרבנן, so the רבנן did not apply it to an אסטניס. It then brings ברייתות about how to treat slaves who die, including רבי אליעזר's story, and about who may be called אבות, אמהות, אבא and אמא. The amud ends with רבי אלעזר's praise of קריאת שמע and תפלה and a list of personal prayers that חכמים said after davening, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only someone marrying a virgin?
steps.stepSummary: If the חתן is exempt because he is busy with a מצוה, then someone marrying an אלמנה should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the reason, why does the משנה talk specifically about someone marrying a בתולה? Even someone marrying an אלמנה should be exempt too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave for the חתן's exemption. If the reason is "busy with a מצוה," it should cover every groom, not just one marrying a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying an אלמנה is just as much a מצוה as marrying a בתולה. So if being busy with a מצוה is what exempts, the משנה's focus on a בתולה looks too narrow. The גמרא wants to know what makes the בתולה case special.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the reason

phrases.english: If so, why specifically
one who marries a virgin?
Even one who marries a widow should also be exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reason (busy with a מצוה) given for the חתן's exemption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's limiting the exemption to one who marries a בתולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the exemption comes from doing a מצוה, marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה, so the limit to a בתולה makes no sense.

steps.title: The virgin's groom is preoccupied, the widow's is not
steps.stepSummary: The difference is preoccupation: the one marrying a בתולה is preoccupied, and the one marrying an אלמנה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (marrying a בתולה) he is preoccupied, and here (marrying an אלמנה) he is not preoccupied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two grooms are not the same. Only the one marrying a בתולה is so preoccupied that he cannot concentrate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being busy with a מצוה is not enough by itself. The exemption also needs real preoccupation (טרדא) that keeps him from focusing on קריאת שמע. That is why the משנה mentions only the בתולה case.

phrases.english: Here, he is preoccupied,
phrases.notes: The first "here" is the groom marrying a בתולה. The second "here" is the groom marrying an אלמנה.

phrases.english: and here, he is not preoccupied.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא טְרִיד וְהָכָא לָא טְרִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by drawing a distinction between the two grooms.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every groom doing the מצוה of marriage should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption also requires preoccupation, which exists only when marrying a בתולה.

steps.title: If preoccupation exempts, why is a mourner obligated?
steps.stepSummary: If preoccupation exempts, then someone whose ship sank should be exempt too. But רב says an אבל is obligated in all the מצוות except תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the reason is preoccupation, then even someone whose ship sank at sea should be exempt. So why did רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: an אבל is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah except תפילין, because they are called "splendor," as it says, "Bind your splendor upon yourself"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. If being preoccupied exempts a person, then anyone who is upset should be exempt, but רב rules that a mourner must still keep the מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone whose ship sank, or an אבל, is clearly very preoccupied. Yet רב's ruling obligates the אבל in every מצוה, with only one exception: תפילין. That exception comes from the word פאר (splendor), not from his being upset. So preoccupation alone does not seem to exempt anyone.
steps.confusionAlert: The תפילין exception does not come from the mourner being upset. It comes only from the word פאר, because "splendor" does not fit a mourner. For everything else, including קריאת שמע, his distress does not exempt him.

phrases.english: If it is because of preoccupation,
then even one whose ship sank at sea should also be exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Why then did Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say in the name of Rav:
A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות
stated in the Torah,
except for tefillin,
since "splendor" is said about them,
as it says: "Bind your splendor upon yourself, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם טִרְדָּא אֲפִילּוּ טָבְעָה סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 (preoccupation exempts) using רב's ruling about an אבל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that preoccupation is what exempts the חתן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mourner, or someone who lost his ship, is very preoccupied, yet רב obligates the mourner in all the מצוות. So preoccupation cannot be what creates an exemption.

steps.title: Preoccupation from a מצוה versus ordinary preoccupation
steps.stepSummary: The mourner's preoccupation is not a מצוה (רשות), while the חתן's preoccupation comes from a מצוה, and only that kind exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: there, it is preoccupation that is not a מצוה. Here, it is preoccupation that comes from a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting preoccupation into two kinds. Only preoccupation caused by doing a מצוה exempts a person from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourner and the ship-owner are upset, but there is no מצוה in being upset, so they stay obligated. The חתן marrying a בתולה is preoccupied because of the מצוה itself, so he is exempt. Both parts are needed: a מצוה and real preoccupation.

keyTerms.meaning: Preoccupation over something that is not a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע only when both parts are present: he is doing a מצוה, and that מצוה makes him truly preoccupied. That is why it applies to marrying a בתולה. Ordinary worry, like grief or losing a ship, does not exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule: worry that comes from a מצוה can exempt a person, but personal worry or sadness does not release him from his obligations.

phrases.english: They say: there, it is preoccupation over something optional,
phrases.notes: "Optional" here just means it is not a מצוה. There is no מצוה in being upset over a loss.

phrases.english: here, it is preoccupation over a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי הָתָם טִרְדָּא דִרְשׁוּת הָכָא טִרְדָּא דְמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by telling apart two kinds of preoccupation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any preoccupation, even grief or financial loss, should exempt a person from מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only preoccupation that comes from a מצוה exempts. Preoccupation that is not a מצוה does not.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל bathes on the night his wife died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that רבן גמליאל bathed on the first night after his wife's death. When his students questioned him, he explained that he is an אסטניס.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He bathed on the first night after his wife died. His students said to him: Didn't you teach us, our teacher, that a mourner may not bathe? He said to them: I am not like other people; I am delicate.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה tells a story where רבן גמליאל seems to break his own rule about an אבל bathing. He explains why his case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אבל may not bathe. רבן גמליאל does not deny the rule. He says he is an אסטניס, someone for whom not bathing causes real physical suffering, so the rule does not apply to him in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: A delicate, sensitive person who suffers physically without bathing

phrases.english: MISHNA: He bathed on the first night
phrases.notes: "He" is רבן גמליאל. The משנה is continuing its stories about him.

phrases.english: after his wife died.
His students said to him:
Didn't you teach us, our teacher,
that a mourner is forbidden to bathe?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם אֵינִי כִּשְׁאָר בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: He said to them: I am not like other people;
I am delicate.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רָחַץ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁמֵּתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the גמרא's discussion of why a חתן is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not bathe, but an אסטניס, for whom not bathing is real suffering, is an exception.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל accepts condolences for his slave טבי
steps.stepSummary: When his slave טבי died, רבן גמליאל accepted תנחומין, even though he taught that one does not accept condolences for slaves. He explained that טבי was an exceptionally worthy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when his slave טבי died, he accepted condolences. His students said to him: Didn't you teach us, our teacher, that one does not accept condolences for slaves? He said to them: My slave טבי is not like all other slaves; he was a worthy person.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story in the same pattern: רבן גמליאל seems to act against his own teaching, and he explains why this case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays in place: no תנחומין for slaves. טבי is treated as an exception because he was כשר, a truly righteous person, so he deserved the respect given to a family member.

keyTerms.meaning: He was a worthy, upright person

phrases.english: And when his slave טבי died,
he accepted condolences for him.
His students said to him:
Didn't you teach us, our teacher,
that one does not accept condolences for slaves?
He said to them: My slave טבי is not
like all the other slaves; he was worthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת טָבִי עַבְדּוֹ קִבֵּל עָלָיו תַּנְחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story with the same structure: an action, a question from the students, and an explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does not accept תנחומין for slaves, but an exceptionally worthy slave like טבי is an exception.

steps.title: May a groom choose to recite קריאת שמע on his first night?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a חתן who wants to recite קריאת שמע on his first night may do so. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees: not everyone who wants to take on a reputation for piety may do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: A groom, if he wants to recite קריאת שמע on the first night, may recite it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Not everyone who wants to take the name may take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה returns to the חתן, who is exempt from קריאת שמע, and records a מחלוקת about whether he may recite it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the חתן is exempt. The question is whether he may be stricter on himself. The תנא קמא allows it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects that this looks like showing off a piety the person may not truly have, since he is too distracted to focus.

keyTerms.meaning: To take the name, meaning to claim a reputation for being especially pious

phrases.english: A groom, if he wants to recite
קריאת שמע on the first night, may recite it.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִיטּוֹל אֶת הַשֵּׁם, יִטּוֹל.
phrases.english: Not everyone who wants to take the name may take it.
phrases.notes: "The name" means a reputation for being a God-fearing person.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָתָן אִם רוֹצֶה לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about רבן גמליאל and returns to the topic of a חתן and קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, an exempt חתן may recite קריאת שמע. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he may not, because it is a false claim to piety.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the general question of whether someone who is exempt may choose to be stricter, or whether doing so can look like showing off.

steps.title: Why was רבן גמליאל allowed to bathe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבן גמליאל bathing as a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first story in the משנה and asks how רבן גמליאל could bathe while in mourning. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "I am delicate" does not explain on its own why a mourning rule could be relaxed. The גמרא wants the legal basis for treating an אסטניס differently.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the last thing the משנה mentioned was רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the חתן, this question is about רבן גמליאל's bathing in step 5.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason
of רבן גמליאל?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves them out. So this is about רבן גמליאל, the one who bathed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Jumps back over steps 6 and 7 to explain the bathing story in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic basis that allowed רבן גמליאל, an אבל, to bathe on the first night.

steps.title: Mourning at night is only rabbinic, and it was never imposed on a delicate person
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that אנינות at night is only דרבנן, based on the פסוק "its end like a bitter day." The רבנן did not apply their rule to an אסטניס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that acute mourning at night is rabbinic, as it is written: "And its end like a bitter day." And in the case of a delicate person, the Sages did not make the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: on the night of the death, the mourning is only rabbinic, and the רבנן made an exception for a delicate person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the mourning a bitter "day," so by Torah law אנינות applies only during the day of the death. The night that follows is a rabbinic addition, and the רבנן never made that rule for an אסטניס. That is why רבן גמליאל could bathe that first night.

keyTerms.meaning: The intense first stage of mourning, before burial or on the day of death
They did not make a decree

steps.whatToRemember: Torah-level אנינות is only by day. At night it is דרבנן, so the רבנן could leave out an אסטניס. This explains why רבן גמליאל bathed.

phrases.english: He holds: acute mourning at night is rabbinic,
as it is written: "And its end like a bitter day."
phrases.notes: עמוס 8:10. The word "day" is the key: by Torah law the mourning applies to the day only.

phrases.english: And in the case of a delicate person,
the Sages did not decree for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר אֲנִינוּת לַיְלָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אנינות at night is only דרבנן, based on "כיום מר", and the רבנן did not apply that rule to an אסטניס.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common principle: a rabbinic rule can make room for real hardship in a way a Torah law might not.

steps.title: No formal mourning rituals for slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about טבי and brings a ברייתא: for slaves, people do not stand in the comforters' row and do not say the mourners' blessing or mourners' comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When טבי his slave died, etc.' The רבנן taught: For male and female slaves who die, people do not stand in a row to comfort the mourners, and they do not say the mourners' blessing or the mourners' comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about טבי. It brings a ברייתא that states the basic rule about mourning for slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out the rule that רבן גמליאל himself had taught. It lists three mourning rituals: the row of comforters, the mourners' blessing, and the words of comfort. None of these are done for a slave. This sets up the background for why רבן גמליאל's behavior needed an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The row of comforters who line up to console the mourners
The mourners' blessing, a special blessing said in the mourners' presence
Words of comfort said to the mourners

phrases.english: "And when טבי his slave died, etc."
The Rabbis taught: For slaves and maidservants,
people do not stand in a row for them,
and they do not say the mourners' blessing for them,
or the mourners' comfort.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's טבי episode by bringing the ברייתא behind רבן גמליאל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Formal mourning rituals (row, mourners' blessing, mourners' comfort) are not done for slaves.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's students keep following him
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אליעזר's maidservant died, his students came to comfort him. He kept moving from room to room to avoid them, and they kept following.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story: רבי אליעזר's maidservant died. His students came in to comfort him. When he saw them, he went up to the upper floor, and they went up after him. He went into the gatehouse, and they went in after him. He went into the banquet hall, and they went in after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the ברייתא's rule being put into practice. This step sets the scene, and the next step gives רבי אליעזר's actual teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר did not want to accept formal comfort for a slave, so he tried to hint to his students by walking away. The students missed the hint and kept following him. This leads him to tell them the rule directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as an example
An upper floor or attic room
A large banquet hall or reception room

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵתָה שִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: There was an incident: רבי אליעזר's maidservant died.
His students came in to comfort him.
As soon as he saw them, he went up to the upper floor,
and they went up after him.
He went into the gatehouse, and they went in after him.
He went into the banquet hall, and they went in after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵתָה שִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that shows the ברייתא's rule in real life.

steps.title: Say to the owner what you would say about a lost animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר scolds his students for missing his hints, repeats the rule, and teaches that for a slave you say 'May המקום fill your loss,' the same thing said about a dead ox or donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I thought you would get burned by lukewarm water, but now you are not burned even by boiling hot water. Did I not teach you this: For slaves and maidservants, people do not stand in a row, and they do not say the mourners' blessing or the mourners' comfort? So what do they say? Just as people say to someone whose ox or donkey died, 'May המקום fill your loss,' so too they say to him about his slave or maidservant, 'May המקום fill your loss.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר tells his students plainly why he was avoiding them. He repeats the ברייתא's rule and adds what you should say instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lukewarm water' image means: I thought a small hint would be enough for you, but even a big hint did not work. The new information is the right wording: the loss of a slave is treated as a money loss, like losing an animal. So the comfort is about refilling a loss, not about mourning a relative.
steps.whatToRemember: For a slave, people do not do mourning rituals. Instead they say, 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך,' the same thing said about a dead animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך' here as the familiar comfort for mourners ('המקום ינחם'). The point is that this is the wording for a money loss, not for mourning a person.

phrases.english: He said to them: I thought
that you would get burned by lukewarm water,
phrases.notes: He means: I thought even a small hint would be enough for you to get the message.

phrases.aramaic: עַכְשָׁיו אִי אַתֶּם נִכְוִים אֲפִילּוּ בְּחַמֵּי חַמִּין,
phrases.english: but now you are not burned even by boiling hot water,
Did I not teach you this:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִים עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה,
phrases.english: For slaves and maidservants, people do not stand in a row for them,
and they do not say the mourners' blessing for them,
nor the mourners' comfort?
So what do people say about them?
Just as people say to a person
about his ox or his donkey that died:
"May המקום fill your loss,"

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ עַל עַבְדּוֹ וְעַל שִׁפְחָתוֹ
phrases.english: so too people say to him about his slave or his maidservant:
"May המקום fill your loss."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָה אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story: רבי אליעזר explains his behavior and adds the proper wording for comfort.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a dead slave, people say 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך,' just as they would for a dead ox or donkey.

steps.title: No eulogy for slaves, with an exception from רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says slaves are not eulogized. רבי יוסי says a worthy slave may be praised as 'a good and faithful man who enjoyed the fruit of his labor.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: Slaves and maidservants are not eulogized. רבי יוסי says: If he was a worthy slave, people say about him, 'Alas, a good and faithful man who enjoyed the fruit of his labor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא, this one about eulogies, along with רבי יוסי's opinion that makes an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא was about comforting the owner. This one is about eulogizing the slave himself. The basic rule is no eulogy, but רבי יוסי allows a short line of praise for a slave who was especially good.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין מַסְפִּידִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.english: Another ברייתא taught: Slaves and maidservants are not eulogized.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם עֶבֶד כָּשֵׁר הוּא —
phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: If he was a worthy slave,
people say about him: "Alas, a good and faithful man
who enjoyed the fruit of his labor."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין מַסְפִּידִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא on a related topic: eulogizing slaves, rather than comforting their owners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves are not eulogized. רבי יוסי allows a short praise for a worthy slave.

steps.title: The חכמים object that רבי יוסי's praise is too high
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יוסי: if that is what you say for a slave, what praise is left for worthy free people?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, what have you left for worthy people?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יוסי's exception from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that the words רבי יוסי suggested are high praise. Even an upright free Jew would be proud to be eulogized that way. So using them for a slave erases the difference the rule is meant to keep. The ברייתא ends with this objection and gives no answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is true

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים's objection. Their view is that even a worthy slave should not get a eulogy that would fit an upright free person.

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
what have you left for the worthy?
phrases.notes: He means worthy free people. Your words for a slave are already the praise they would get.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, מָה הִנַּחְתָּ לַכְּשֵׁרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יוסי's exception in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's suggested eulogy for a worthy slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His wording is the praise fit for worthy free people. Using it for a slave leaves nothing higher to say for them.

steps.title: Only three are called 'fathers' and only four 'mothers'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only three people are called אבות and only four are called אמהות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We call only three people 'fathers' (אבות), and we call only four women 'mothers' (אמהות).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who gets the special title אבות or אמהות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title אבות goes only to אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב, not to יעקב's sons. The title אמהות goes only to שרה, רבקה, רחל, and לאה. This sets up the question in the next step: why stop there?

keyTerms.meaning: The fathers of the Jewish people
The mothers of the Jewish people
We do not call (someone by a title)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We call only three people "fathers,"
and we call only four women "mothers."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין קוֹרִין ״אָבוֹת״ אֶלָּא לִשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of how to honor slaves after death to a new ברייתא about honorific titles, which will lead back to slaves in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The title אבות is only for three people, and the title אמהות is only for four.

steps.title: Why only three fathers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that only three people are called אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for the rule about the fathers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why יעקב's sons are not also called אבות. This question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what logic limits the title to exactly three people.

phrases.english: Regarding the fathers, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבוֹת מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the title אבות stops at יעקב and is not given to his sons.

steps.title: A suggested reason fails because of the mothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests we don't call the שבטים 'fathers' because we don't know which one we come from, but rejects this, since the same doubt applies to רחל and לאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because we don't know whether we come from ראובן or from שמעון, then the same is true of the mothers: we don't know whether we come from רחל or from לאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer and then shows it can't be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion: we can't say 'our father ראובן' because we don't know which tribe we come from. But רחל and לאה raise the same doubt, and they are still called אמהות. So uncertainty about descent can't be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is because we do not know
whether we come from ראובן
or whether we come from שמעון,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי אִמָּהוֹת נָמֵי לָא יָדְעִינַן
phrases.english: if so, with the mothers too we do not know
whether we come from רחל
or whether we come from לאה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 16 and immediately rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggested reason only, not the rule of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same doubt about descent exists for רחל and לאה, who are still called אמהות, so the doubt can't explain the rule.

steps.title: Only up to יעקב are they important enough
steps.stepSummary: The real reason: the people up to יעקב are important enough for the title אבות, and those after him are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, up to here (יעקב) they are important enough; beyond that they are not important enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to why only three are called אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is about importance, not about knowing who we descend from. אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב have a special status that the שבטים do not have for this title.
steps.whatToRemember: The titles אבות and אמהות depend on importance. Only the three אבות and four אמהות are important enough for them.

phrases.english: Rather, up to here they are important,
phrases.notes: "Up to here" means up to and including יעקב.

phrases.english: beyond that they are not important.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, עַד הָכָא חֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from step 17 with the accepted answer to step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only those up to יעקב are important enough to be called אבות.

steps.title: Slaves are not called 'אבא' or 'אמא', but רבן גמליאל's were
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says slaves and maidservants are not called 'אבא פלוני' or 'אמא פלונית', yet רבן גמליאל's slaves were called that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: Slaves and maidservants are not called 'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so.' But the slaves of רבן גמליאל were called 'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about honorific titles, this time for slaves. It sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Older people were often honored with the title 'אבא' or 'אמא', but the ברייתא says not to use it for slaves. Then the same ברייתא reports that people did use it for רבן גמליאל's slaves, which looks like a contradiction.

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא:
Slaves and maidservants, we do not call them
"Father so-and-so" and "Mother so-and-so."

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיוּ קוֹרִים אוֹתָם
phrases.english: But those of רבן גמליאל, they would call them
"Father so-and-so" and "Mother so-and-so."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידָךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין קוֹרִין אוֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of titles from step 15, now applied to slaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves are not given the titles אבא and אמא, but רבן גמליאל's slaves were.

steps.title: How can a story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can state a rule and then tell a story that goes against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a story brought to contradict the rule?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the story about רבן גמליאל's slaves seems to go against the rule stated right before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a story is brought to support a rule, not to break it. Here the rule says slaves are not called 'אבא', and the story says they were.

keyTerms.meaning: A story brought to contradict? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: A story to contradict?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה לִסְתּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 19, which states a rule and then a story that breaks it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should support the rule it follows. Here it seems to contradict it.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's slaves were especially important
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבן גמליאל's slaves were called by these titles because they were important.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because they were important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story is an exception, not a contradiction: these slaves were important people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for ordinary slaves stays the same. רבן גמליאל's slaves were known as worthy and respected, so they earned the honorific titles. This matches the idea from step 18 that titles depend on importance.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות follow one idea: honorific titles depend on how important a person is. Ordinary slaves don't get them, but רבן גמליאל's important slaves did.

phrases.english: Because they were important.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: the story is a special exception, not a break in the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to show that slaves may be called 'אבא' and 'אמא', against the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule holds for ordinary slaves. רבן גמליאל's slaves were an exception because they were important.

steps.title: A פסוק that hints to קריאת שמע and תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the two halves of a פסוק in תהלים refer to קריאת שמע and to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What does the פסוק "So I will bless You as I live, to Your name I will raise my hands" mean? "So I will bless You as I live" is קריאת שמע. "To Your name I will raise my hands" is תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר, who reads a פסוק in תהלים as describing two daily מצוות‎: קריאת שמע and תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts, and רבי אלעזר matches each part to one practice. The first half, "So I will bless You as I live," is קריאת שמע. The second half, "to Your name I will raise my hands," is תפלה, since raising one's hands is a picture of praying.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (introduces an explanation of a פסוק)
Prayer; in the גמרא this usually means the שמונה עשרה
I will raise my hands (a picture of praying)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"So I will bless You as I live,
to Your name I will raise my hands"?
"So I will bless You as I live":
this is the reading of שמע.
"To Your name I will raise my hands":
this is prayer.
phrases.notes: Here "prayer" means the שמונה עשרה, the standing prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic of encouragement about prayer, after the discussion of who may be called אבא and אמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק "כן אברכך בחיי בשמך אשא כפי" refers to קריאת שמע and תפלה.

steps.title: The reward for saying שמע and davening
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that whoever says קריאת שמע and davens will be fully satisfied and will inherit both עולם הזה and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person does this, the פסוק says about him: "As with fat and marrow my soul will be satisfied." More than that, he inherits two worlds, this world and the World to Come, as it says: "And with lips of joys my mouth will praise."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר keeps reading the next פסוק in the same chapter of תהלים to show the reward for someone who says קריאת שמע and תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק speaks of being satisfied as if from rich food, so it describes the reward. Then רבי אלעזר goes a step further: the word רננות, "joys," is plural. That points to two joys, the joy of עולם הזה and the joy of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat and marrow (a picture of rich, satisfying food)
And not only that, but more
This world and the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר teaches that קריאת שמע and תפלה together bring great reward, both in עולם הזה and in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: And if he does so,
phrases.notes: He means: if he says קריאת שמע and also davens.

phrases.english: about him the verse says:
"As with fat and marrow my soul will be satisfied."
And not only that, but
he inherits two worlds:
this world and the World to Come,
as it is said:
"And with lips of joys my mouth will praise."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's teaching by reading the next פסוק as describing the reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who says קריאת שמע and davens is fully satisfied and inherits עולם הזה and עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's personal prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records the prayer רבי אלעזר added after finishing his תפלה, asking for love, students, a good end, גן עדן, a good friend, and a good יצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי אלעזר finished his prayer, he said: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You let love, brotherhood, peace, and friendship live in our lot. May You fill our borders with students, give us success at the end, with a future and hope. Place our portion in גן עדן, and give us a good friend and a good יצר in Your world. May we rise early and find our hearts longing to fear Your name, and may our souls' wishes come before You for good."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins a short list of personal prayers that אמוראים added after the תפלה, starting with רבי אלעזר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an argument. It is a record of what a great Sage asked for in his own words. His requests cover getting along with others, Torah passing on to students, a good end, spiritual help like a good friend and a good יצר, and a heart that wants to fear ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be Your will (opening of a personal request)
The satisfaction or wishes of our souls

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You let dwell in our lot
love and brotherhood, peace and friendship.
And may You fill our borders with many students
and make our end successful, with a future and hope.
And may You place our portion in Gan Eden,
and set us up with a good friend
and a good inclination in Your world.
And may we rise early and find
our hearts longing to fear Your name,
and may the wishes of our souls come before You for good."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After praising תפלה, the גמרא records personal prayers Sages added at its end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר's added prayer: יהי רצון ... שתשכן בפורינו אהבה ואחוה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's personal prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asked ה׳ to see our shame and troubles and to act toward us with His mercy, strength, kindness, grace, goodness, and humility.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי יוחנן finished his prayer, he said: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You look at our shame and see our troubles. Clothe Yourself in Your mercy, cover Yourself with Your strength, wrap Yourself in Your kindness, and gird Yourself with Your grace. May Your goodness and humility come before You."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with the prayer רבי יוחנן said after his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר asked mainly for good things in our lives. רבי יוחנן focuses on ה׳'s side: he asks ה׳ to notice our low state and to "dress" Himself in His kind qualities when He deals with us. The pictures of clothing, covering, and wrapping describe ה׳ acting with mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: That You look at, peek at
And gird Yourself, put on like a belt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You look at our shame,
and see our troubles,
and clothe Yourself in Your mercy,
and cover Yourself with Your strength,
and wrap Yourself in Your kindness,
and gird Yourself with Your grace,
and may Your quality of goodness and humility come before You."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the list of personal prayers after תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's added prayer: יהי רצון ... שתציץ בבשתנו ותביט ברעתנו.

steps.title: רבי זירא's personal prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא's short prayer asked that we not sin, not be ashamed, and not embarrass ourselves before our fathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי זירא finished his prayer, he said: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that we not sin, not be ashamed, and not be embarrassed before our fathers."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third personal prayer, the short one רבי זירא said after his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's request is short and focused: that we stay away from sin. Sin brings shame, and he asks that our actions never embarrass us in front of our אבות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that we not sin and not be ashamed
and not be embarrassed before our fathers."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list of personal prayers after תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא's added prayer: יהי רצון ... שלא נחטא ולא נבוש ולא נכלם מאבותינו.

steps.title: רבי חייא's prayer that תורה be our life's work
steps.stepSummary: After davening, רבי חייא asked that תורה be our occupation, and that our heart not grow faint and our eyes not grow dim.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי חייא davened, he said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that Your תורה be our occupation, that our heart not become faint, and that our eyes not grow dim.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more personal prayer to its list, this time from רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier prayers asked for things like a good friend or a good יצר. רבי חייא focuses on תורה as his main work in life. He also asks for the strength, in heart and in eyes, to keep going.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be Your will. The standard opening of a personal request.
A craft or trade, one's main occupation

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya, after he prayed, said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that Your Torah be our occupation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יִדְוֶה לִבֵּנוּ, וְאַל יֶחְשְׁכוּ עֵינֵינוּ״.
phrases.english: and may our heart not become faint, and may our eyes not grow dim."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sage's post-תפלה prayer to the list that began in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא prayed that תורה be our occupation and that our heart and eyes stay strong.

steps.title: רב's prayer for a long and full life
steps.stepSummary: After davening, רב asked for a long life filled with peace, goodness, blessing, livelihood, יראת חטא, honor, love of תורה, and the fulfillment of our heart's good wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his תפלה, רב said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You give us a long life. Let it be a life of peace, goodness, blessing, and livelihood. A life of physical strength, a life with fear of sin, a life without shame or disgrace, a life of wealth and honor, a life in which we love תורה and fear Heaven, and a life in which You fulfill all our heart's wishes for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records רב's personal prayer after davening, which asks for many different kinds of 'life.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב builds his prayer around the word חיים, and each line describes another quality of a good life. It moves from physical needs like livelihood and strength to spiritual ones like יראת חטא and אהבת תורה. This is the prayer we now say in ברכת החודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'loosening of the bones.' Vigor and physical strength, or freedom of movement.

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer became part of the ברכת החודש said on the שבת before ראש חודש, with an opening line added.

phrases.english: Rav, after his prayer, said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You give us long life,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם, חַיִּים שֶׁל טוֹבָה,
phrases.english: a life of peace, a life of goodness,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁל בְּרָכָה, חַיִּים שֶׁל פַּרְנָסָה,
phrases.english: a life of blessing, a life of livelihood,
a life of strength of the bones,
a life in which there is fear of sin,
a life in which there is no shame or disgrace,
a life of wealth and honor,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁתְּהֵא בָּנוּ אַהֲבַת תּוֹרָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: a life in which we have love of Torah and fear of Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁתְּמַלֵּא לָנוּ אֶת כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבֵּנוּ לְטוֹבָה״.
phrases.english: a life in which You fulfill for us all the wishes of our heart for good."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of personal prayers with רב's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב prayed for a long life that is full in body, livelihood, honor, and spirit.

steps.title: רבי's prayer for protection from harmful people and things
steps.stepSummary: After davening, רבי יהודה הנשיא asked to be saved from arrogant people and from arrogance, from bad people, bad events, a bad יצר, bad friends and neighbors, the destroying שטן, harsh judgment, and harsh opponents, whether Jewish or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his תפלה, רבי said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God and God of our fathers, that You save us from arrogant people and from arrogance, from a bad person and a bad mishap, from a bad יצר, a bad friend, a bad neighbor, and the destroying שטן, from a harsh judgment and a harsh opponent in court, whether he is a Jew or not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records the personal prayer of רבי יהודה הנשיא, which is a list of things he asked to be protected from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב asked for good things, while רבי asks to be kept away from harm. His list covers people (arrogant ones, bad friends and neighbors), forces (the יצר הרע and the שטן), and legal danger (a harsh judgment or a harsh opponent). We say this prayer each morning at the end of ברכות השחר.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad mishap or harmful encounter
An opposing party in a court case
Member of the covenant, meaning a Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer appears in the סידור as the daily 'יהי רצון' at the end of ברכות השחר.

phrases.english: Rebbi, after his prayer, said this:

phrases.aramaic: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ,
phrases.english: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God and God of our fathers,
that You save us from arrogant people and from arrogance,
from a bad person, and from a bad mishap,
from an evil inclination, from a bad friend,
from a bad neighbor, and from the destroying Satan,
and from a harsh judgment and from a harsh opponent in court,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהוּא בֶּן בְּרִית בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּן בְּרִית״.
phrases.english: whether he is a member of the covenant or whether he is not a member of the covenant."
phrases.notes: "Member of the covenant" means a Jew. "He" is the harsh opponent in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with רבי's prayer, which asks for protection instead of blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי prayed to be protected from arrogance, bad people and influences, the שטן, and harsh judgment.

steps.title: רבי prayed this even though guards protected him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי said this prayer even though government officers stood guard over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said this even though royal officers stood guard over רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short comment about רבי's prayer from the step before. It points out that he asked for protection even though he already had guards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a man protected by royal guards would not need to pray about arrogant people or harsh opponents. The גמרא teaches that he still prayed, because human protection is no substitute for asking ה׳ for help.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers or guards, here the royal guards assigned to רבי

steps.whatToRemember: So far the גמרא has listed the personal prayers of רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן, רבי זירא, רבי חייא, רב, and רבי, and the list continues with רב ספרא in the next step. Some of these prayers became part of our סידור. רבי prayed for protection even though he had guards.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָיְימִי קָצוֹצֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי.
phrases.english: And this was even though officers stood over Rebbi.
phrases.notes: These were government guards who protected רבי. He still asked ה׳ to protect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָיְימִי קָצוֹצֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A comment on step 29 that shows how serious רבי's prayer for protection was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי prayed for protection every day even though royal guards protected him.

steps.title: רב ספרא's prayer begins with a request for peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the personal prayer that רב ספרא said after his תפילה, which opens by asking ה׳ to establish peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רב ספרא said this: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You establish peace..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another name to its list of חכמים and their after-davening prayers. Here it starts quoting רב ספרא's prayer, and the rest of the prayer follows next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The format is the same as the earlier entries: a חכם's name, the words "after his prayer he said this," and then the prayer itself. רב ספרא opens with the familiar formula יהי רצון and asks first for שלום (peace). The specific kinds of peace he asks for come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: After his prayer, meaning after finishing the עמידה
He said this, which introduces a quote
May it be Your will, the standard opening of a personal request

phrases.english: Rav Safra, after his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You establish peace

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another entry to the list of after-davening prayers that the חכמים said. It follows רבי's prayer in steps 29-30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא's personal prayer after davening opens with a request that ה׳ establish peace.
